t.5.59.1: Then the forest-dwellers, the heroes led by Aṅgada, and Hanumān, the great monkey, accepted the words of Jāmbavān.
t.5.59.2: Then all those bulls among the leaping monkeys, filled with joy and led by the son of Vāyu, left the summit of Mahendra and leapt forth.
t.5.59.3: Resembling Meru and Mandara, like great elephants in rut, those mighty ones of enormous bodies seemed to cover the very sky.
t.5.59.5: Having secured the accomplishment of the purpose for Rāghava and supreme glory for our master, we, our aims fulfilled, stand exalted by the success of our deeds.
t.5.59.4: With their eyes they seem to carry, as it were, that Hanumān, self-possessed, of great strength and great speed, who was being honored by all beings.
t.5.59.6: All of them were eager to relate the pleasing news, all of them delighted in the prospect of battle, and all of them, high-spirited, were firmly resolved upon redressing the wrong done to Rāma.
t.5.59.7: Then those forest-dwellers, leaping and springing up into the sky, reached a grove like Nandana, filled with trees and creepers.
t.5.59.8: That grove named Madhuvana, guarded by Sugrīva, was unassailable by all beings and enchanting to the minds of all creatures.
t.5.59.9: That which is ever guarded by the monkey Dadhimukha of great valour, the maternal uncle of the great-souled Sugrīva, chief of the monkeys.
t.5.59.10: Having reached that great forest, most dear to the heart of the lord of the vānaras, those vānaras became exceedingly wild with excitement.
t.5.59.11: Then those monkeys, tawny as honey, delighted at the sight of the great Madhuvana, begged the prince for the honey.
t.5.59.12: Then the prince, having obtained the consent of those elder monkeys headed by Jāmbavān, gave them leave to feast on the honey.
t.5.59.13: Then, having received permission, all the forest-dwellers were thrilled with delight; and then, rejoicing, they danced about here and there.
t.5.59.14: Some sing, some bow low, some dance, some laugh aloud; some fall down, some wander about, some leap, and some chatter wildly.
t.5.59.15: Some leaned upon one another, some shouted boastfully at one another; some leapt from tree to tree, and some dropped to the ground from the tops of the trees.
t.5.59.16: Some, their speed aroused, leap up from the surface of the earth to the tops of the great trees; one, laughing, approaches another who is singing, and another, laughing, approaches one who is laughing.
t.5.59.17: One, weeping loudly, approaches another who weeps; one, shoving hard, approaches another who shoves. That army of monkeys was in utter turmoil, its spirits and antics wild from drinking the honey; there was no one there who was not drunk, and no one there who was not sated.
t.5.59.18: Then, seeing that grove being devoured and its trees stripped of their leaves and flowers, the monkey named Dadhivaktra, in anger, tried to hold back those monkeys.
t.5.59.19: Threatened by those emboldened monkeys, the guardian of the forest, the eldest of the monkey heroes, fierce in his energy, once more set his mind on protecting the forest from the vānaras.
t.5.59.20: To some he spoke harsh words, boldly and without restraint, and others he struck with his palms; meeting with some, he picked a quarrel, and likewise he approached some with conciliation.
t.5.59.21: He was assailed by them, whose onrush was irresistible through intoxication and who, because of their strength, could not be held back by him; and the fearless ones, closing in together, dragged him about without regard for the wrong they did.
t.5.59.22: Scratching him with their nails, biting him with their teeth, and setting upon him with their palms and feet, all the monkeys, in their intoxication, assailed that monkey, and they stripped the great forest bare.
